I am 70 years old, and I have farmed this land for 56 years. I only finished primary school, but I know this 4.1 mu field better than any book. Last year I grew spring peanut on the whole plot using an improved variety — Huayu, the same seed my neighbor Old Zhang used — and I got about 550 jin per mu. That was enough to cover my costs and leave some money for me and my wife, so I will do the same this year. I need about 100 jin of seed pods for the whole plot.

For fertilizer, I will buy three 50kg bags of compound fertilizer from the dealer in town. That is about 170 yuan per bag, so 510 yuan total. Last year I only used two bags, but by July the leaves looked a little yellow, so this year I am adding one more bag to be safe. I spread it all as base fertilizer before sowing. When the plants flower, I will also spread half a bag of urea — about 25 kg — because I have seen that extra nitrogen at flowering helps the pods fill out. Peanut can make its own nitrogen, but I would rather waste a little fertilizer than risk a bad harvest. A bad year is a disaster; extra fertilizer is just a cost.

I have a well, and I will irrigate twice. The first time is right after sowing in early May if the soil is dry. The second time is in mid-July when the flowers set pods and the weather turns hot. Pumping water costs diesel and my old legs can only manage so much, so twice is my plan.

For pests, I spray three times. The dealer mixes fungicide and insecticide for me in one bottle. I spray first when the leaves start spotting in late June, then again after heavy rain, and a third time in August before the pods finish filling. That is what everyone around here does.

For tillage, I hire the man with the rotary tiller. He charges about 30 yuan per mu and he did a good job last year. I am too old to plow with an animal now.

I expect about 280 kg per mu this year if the rain comes at the right time. That is about 2,300 jin total from my 4.1 mu.
